prompt.brief: Design a hybrid-cloud platform that manages on-premises and public-cloud resources with private connectivity, consistent identity and policy, unified observability, and safe workload placement.
successSignals: Separate desired resource and policy state from provider observations, local control planes, network routes, and workload data.
Use adapters and asynchronous reconciliation so cloud API failure or a disconnected site cannot corrupt desired state.
Enforce identity, encryption, residency, segmentation, and policy consistently while allowing provider-specific capabilities.
Explain bandwidth constraints, split-brain connectivity, certificate rotation, disaster recovery, placement, and auditability.

functional: Register sites and cloud accounts, discover resources, apply declarative policies, provision services, and manage private routes.
Expose desired versus observed state, connectivity, policy drift, capacity, health, and deployment operation progress.
Support role-based access, secrets and certificate rotation, workload migration, backup, site isolation, and audit export.
nonFunctional: Target p95 control-plane status latency below 500 ms and keep application traffic within a site-specific network budget.
Manage thousands of resources across cloud accounts and disconnected sites with site-scoped queues and policy workers.
Make reconciliation, provisioning, policy evaluation, and certificate operations idempotent and auditable.
Serve last-known state and queue changes during link loss while preventing unsafe cross-boundary mutations.
scaleAssumptions: Manage 50 sites, 20 cloud accounts, and 100,000 resources with intermittent links and regional policy differences.
Partition desired and observed state by site, account, tenant, and provider; isolate disconnected or noisy sites.
Retain encrypted policy decisions, resource snapshots, connectivity events, and audit records for replay.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Hybrid-cloud platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Hybrid-cloud platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Hybrid-cloud platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Hybrid-cloud platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Hybrid-cloud platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Hybrid-cloud platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Hybrid-cloud platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Hybrid-cloud platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Hybrid-cloud platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
